title: Optional per-substrate config: [substrates.local] and [substrates.cloud] overlay the whole runners.toml
description:
OPERATOR, 2026-09-23: 'the config system should support different configs for cloud and local (optional)'. Prompted by: 'if a tick is complex you can consider using a claude executor locally. It should be significantly stronger than pi/glm' - and the cloud must never run claude.

TODAY: 84z (xte) added roles.<role>.substrates.cloud, a per-ROLE overlay only. Two gaps:
  1. Nothing else is substrate-aware. [tier_policy] (default, ceiling, step, start rules) and the tier DEFINITIONS are global, so 'locally a failed GLM tick climbs to claude; in the cloud it stops at GLM' cannot be said.
  2. Precedence is backwards for safety. 84z's own comment: 'a tier still the more specific axis' - a tier overlay applies OVER the cloud overlay, so a frontier tier naming claude would win in a cloud run (finding ea1a62d3).

DESIGN:
  - An OPTIONAL [substrates.<name>] table that mirrors the top-level schema. When the run's substrate matches, its tables overlay the base field-wise. No [substrates.*] = behaviour unchanged.
  - Names: 'cloud' is the container substrate; 'local' covers every non-cloud substrate (auto, herdr, harness). A config naming another key is refused with the list.
  - SCOPE, not just override: a tier defined under one substrate does not exist in the other. A cloud run cannot name a tier that only [substrates.local] defines - so 'frontier = claude, local only' is expressible and safe by construction.
  - The substrate overlay applies LAST, after the tier overlay. That closes ea1a62d3 by construction.
  - 84z's roles.<x>.substrates.cloud keeps working, as sugar for substrates.cloud.roles.<x>; both forms naming the same field is refused rather than silently ordered.

UPSTREAM: tk's own copy of the runners config refuses unknown keys - ticks uep (already filed for 84z's form) must learn [substrates.*] too, or tk commands fail in this repository.

FIRST USE, once this lands: [substrates.local.roles.implement.tiers.frontier] kind = claude, model = opus; [substrates.local.tier_policy] default = strong, ceiling = frontier; [substrates.cloud.tier_policy] ceiling = strong.
acceptance_criteria: runners.toml accepts optional [substrates.local] and [substrates.cloud] overlays of the whole schema; with none, resolution is unchanged; a tier defined only under one substrate is unknown to the other and naming it there is refused; the substrate overlay is applied after the tier overlay, proven by a test where a local-only claude frontier tier is unreachable from a cloud run; 84z's roles.<x>.substrates.cloud still works and conflicting duplicate forms are refused; and the full suites pass
